To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adduct level in DNA of lacI transgene mice fed 2-amino 3,4-dmethylimidazo [4,5-f ] quinoline (MeIQ) was highest in the liver, and that the mutagenicity of MeIQ was highest in the large intestine, where DNA synthesis was also highest.

the mutational types and adduct molecular types in the liver, forestomach, bone marrow, heart and colon of Big Blue mice fed a diet containing MeIQ are different from each other and that the adduct level in each organ is correlated with cell proliferation rate.

the DNA adduct level of MeIQ in Big Blue mouse tissues is highest in the liver, and then heart, forestomach, bone marrow and colon in decreasing order, and that no correlation was observed between adduct level in the various tissues and MF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between adduct formation and mutation induction by a food-borne carcinogen in vivo.
the molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis induced by MeIQ.
the relationship between DNA adduct level and lacI MF in various organs of Big Blue mice fed a diet containing a food-borne carcinogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mutational type in the liver, forestomach, bone marrow and heart is not determined by adduct molecular type, that the mutagenicity in the liver, colon, foresto-mach, and bone marrow is not determined by the adduct level, and that the MF may not be determined by adduct level alone.
the MF in various organs is not determined only by adduct levels.
adduct level does not correlate with mutation type, and that adduct level and mutation type do not correlate with MF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MeIQ induced mutations in various tissues, but the mutation spectrum was tissue-specific and the mutation frequency was not correlated with the DNA adduct level.
the MF is not directly related to DNA adduct levels and that the mutagenicity of MeIQ in mice is not explained only by the adduct formation.
the MF is the result of the balance of DNA replication rate, DNA repair and cell loss rate, and adduct formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adduct level does not always correlate with MF, and therefore adduct level is not a good predictor of MF in vivo. © 1999 Wiley-Liss, Inc.
the MF in the liver, colon, foresto-mach and bone marrow of Big Blue mice fed a diet containing MeIQ is not correlated with the DNA adduct level, but is related to cell proliferation.

the MF in the liver, forestomach, heart and bone marrow was 10-60%, and the adduct level in the liver was 28.3 molecule/10(9) nucleotides, whereas the MF in the colon was 2.4-3.2-fold higher, and the adduct levels in the heart and colon were only 0.4 and 3.3 molecule/ 10(9) respectively.
